note: Ranked briefs for root allocation. Root allocates each hypothesis separately; this breadth screen performed no extended attacks. Each brief states quantifiers/definitions, source and duplicate/prior status, mechanism, decisive calculation (already executed under caps), certificate size, formal interfaces, and the strongest routine-adaptation objection.

proposals.title: Explicit universal bound for symmetric point configurations on the sphere
proposals.source: Itai Benjamini, 'Points in Equilibrium' (May 2015), problem sheet equilibrium.pdf; live URL 404 (2026-10-31), preserved copy arquivo.pt/wayback/20201231041612id_/... retained at sources/389505/equilibrium-extracted.md
proposals.statement: A finite subset X of S^2 is symmetric if a finite group acts transitively on X by isometries of the metric space. Known (Benjamini-Finucane-Tessera arXiv:1203.5624, via Breuillard-Green-Tao) that symmetric finite sets NOT on a great circle or two parallel circles have universally bounded size, but no explicit bound. Question: explicit universal upper bound; is the 60-point truncated icosahedron vertex set largest?
proposals.quantifiers_and_definitions: For every finite X subset S^2 such that (i) some finite group G acts transitively on X by isometries (X with its chordal metric; geodesic metric gives the same group), (ii) X is not contained in a great circle and not contained in the union of two parallel circles: bound |X|. Answer: |X| <= 120, attained.
proposals.mechanism: Two elementary lemmas plus a classical classification. (L1, extension lemma) For v_i in X subset R^3, an intrinsic isometry sigma preserves chord distances, hence inner products <v_i,v_j> = 1 - |v_i-v_j|^2/2; the Gram matrix is sigma-invariant, so T(v_i)=v_{sigma(i)} extends to a well-defined orthogonal map of span(X): the transitive group embeds in O(3) and X is a single orbit of a finite G <= O(3). (L2) Finite subgroups of O(3) have order <= 120 (reduce to SO(3) by index <= 2; classical cyclic/dihedral/tetrahedral/octahedral/icosahedral classification). Hence |X| = |G|/|Stab| <= 120. Axial groups (cyclic/dihedral incl. C_nv, C_nh, S_2n, D_n, D_nh, D_nd) have every orbit on <= 2 latitudes, so admissible X come from polyhedral-type groups; the largest orbits avoiding two parallel circles are the generic orbits of I_h.
proposals.decisive_calculation: Executed exactly in Q(sqrt5) (sources/389505/orbit-120-calculation.json, script work/verify_389505.py): binary icosahedral group 2I generated exactly (120 unit quaternions in Q(sqrt5)); orbit of p=(2,3,6) (|p|=7, so normalized points lie on S^2) under I_h = {+/-R} has exactly 120 distinct points, with 30 distinct z-values (so not on any two parallel circles) and the orbit spans R^3 (exact determinant -125/2 + (87/2)sqrt5 != 0, so not on a great circle). Trivial stabilizer verified by orbit size = 120. Hence 60 is NOT largest; the explicit universal bound is 120.
proposals.certificate_size: Small: two short lemmas (extension ~5 lines; bound ~3 lines citing the classical classification) + one explicit 120-point configuration with exact coordinates (120 integer vectors of norm 49, or orbit description via 2 generators + exact orbit table, a few KB).
proposals.formal_interfaces: Needs: finite subgroups of O(3) classification or just max order 120 (orbit-stabilizer + SU(2)/SO(3) facts); linear algebra (Gram matrices, extension of isometries); rational/golden-ratio arithmetic. No analysis. Lean: straightforward with Mathlib's real inner product spaces; the classical classification is the heaviest dependency (could instead prove max order 120 directly from the orbit-of-poles argument, self-contained).
proposals.duplicate_prior_status: Primary body checked (retained). Benjamini-Finucane-Tessera give only a non-explicit bound; Pansu slides (retained) restate it as open. No source found stating the explicit bound 120 or the extension lemma; bounded search only (Exa 429 on 2 queries), no exhaustive registry clearance claimed.
proposals.strongest_routine_adaptation_objection: One might object this is a routine corollary of the classical O(3) classification. It is not automatic: the hypothesis's isometries are of the intrinsic metric space, and the extension lemma (intrinsic isometry => ambient orthogonal map) is the substantive step; also the proposer's 60-point guess is wrong under the literal statement, so the published-record answer is new. If root instead reads 'isometries' as orientation-preserving only, the bound becomes 60 and the truncated icosahedron is co-largest - also a complete answer, smaller still.

proposals.title: A dynamic-programming interval problem (all-k shortest intervals)
proposals.source: Jeff Erickson, Open Algorithmic Problems, 'A dynamic programming problem [David Eppstein]', https://jeffe.cs.illinois.edu/open/algo.html (retained; footer 05 Sep 97; index carries an unexplained 'Progress!' marker - caveat).
proposals.statement: Given a sorted list x_0 <= ... <= x_{n-1} of n real numbers, compute for every 1 <= k <= n the shortest interval containing exactly k entries. (Exactly = contains a consecutive block of k entries; optimal interval endpoints can be shrunk to data points, so the answer for k is m(k) = min_i (x_{i+k-1} - x_i).) Task: a subquadratic algorithm, or a superlinear lower bound in some reasonable model of computation.
proposals.quantifiers_and_definitions: For all n and all sorted real inputs; output the n values m(1),...,m(n) exactly. Equivalent gap form: with d_i = x_{i+1}-x_i and P prefix sums, m(l+1) = min_i (P_{i+l} - P_i) = min-sum contiguous subarray of exact length l.
proposals.mechanism: Divide & conquer on k needs the argmin over i to be monotone in k; exact control C3 shows M[i][k]=P_{i+k-1}-P_i satisfies the Monge inequality on cell (i,k) iff P is convex at index i+k, so monotonicity - and an O(n log n) D&C - is valid on the convex-gap subfamily (verified exactly, control C4), but fails in general (control C2: x=(0,1,2,100,101) has argmin_k2=3 > argmin_k3=0). Attack routes for the delegate: (a) push the subquadratic algorithm beyond convexity via partial-Monge/kinetic or envelope techniques on the n monotone candidate sequences; (b) prove a superlinear lower bound in the algebraic decision tree / comparison model, e.g. by reducing a hard problem to recovering the vector (m(k))_k, or connect to the known difficulty of (min,+)-convolution since m is a self min-plus correlation of a sorted sequence; either endpoint is a publishable full-scope outcome.
proposals.decisive_calculation: Executed exactly (sources/388271/controls-result.json, script work/verify_388271.py): C1 O(n^2) baseline verified, output monotone in k; C2 explicit argmin-monotonicity counterexample; C3 exact equivalence of the Monge cell inequality with pointwise convexity; C4 D&C == brute force on a convex instance (n=12, exact Fractions).
proposals.certificate_size: Algorithm route: proof of the structural lemma + pseudocode, ~2-4 pages; verification certificate is the code plus n log n running-time bound. Lower-bound route: model definition + adversary/reduction, ~3-6 pages.
proposals.formal_interfaces: Algorithm route: sorting/arrays, prefix sums, divide and conquer with monotone argmin - formalizable in Lean with moderate effort (no heavy libraries). Lower-bound route: formalizing a computation model is itself the main cost; a 3SUM-style conditional statement is cheaper but then not an unconditional theorem.
proposals.duplicate_prior_status: Primary page retained; no published subquadratic algorithm or superlinear lower bound found in bounded search (2026-10-31). The 'Progress!' marker on the index is unexplained and is the main prior-art risk; chronology check against Erickson's page history and any follow-up literature is mandatory before acceptance.
proposals.strongest_routine_adaptation_objection: The convex case is routine Monge-array technology, and a reviewer may call the general case 'just SMAWK with a twist' - the counter is control C2: the matrix is genuinely non-Monge on non-convex inputs and two candidate sequences can cross Omega(n) times, so standard column-minimum machinery does not transfer. Conversely a lower-bound claim must name its model precisely; 'dynamic programming is not a reasonable model' per the source.

proposals.title: General polynomials and real-rootedness (AIM Polypartition Problem 2.3)
proposals.source: AIM 'Polyhedral geometry and partition theory' problem list, http://aimpl.org/polypartition/2/ Problem 2.3 (retained; verbatim match; no posted updates).
proposals.statement: Let sum_{i=0}^n b_i x^i be real-rooted with b_i >= 0 and let A_i denote the i-th Eulerian polynomial (A_0=A_1=1, A_2=1+x, A_3=1+4x+x^2, ...). Is sum b_i A_i(x) real-rooted? Determine in general or for particular families.
proposals.quantifiers_and_definitions: Quantified over all real-rooted coefficient vectors b >= 0 (any n). Answer to the literal question: NO.
proposals.mechanism: Exact counterexample: f(z) = (z+5)^3 = z^3+15z^2+75z+125 gives sum b_i A_i = x^2+19x+216 with discriminant -503 < 0 (also x^2+19x+91, disc -3, if A_0 is omitted). General family: for f=(z+t)^3 the discriminant is 12+12t-3t^2, negative for t > 2+2 sqrt(2).
proposals.decisive_calculation: Executed exactly (work/verify_384757.py; results in sources/384757/counterexample-calculation.json; exact Fractions + exact Sturm): Q = x^2+19x+216 has 0 real roots; distinct-root perturbation (z+49/10)(z+5)(z+51/10) -> x^2+19x+107.94, disc -12569/25 < 0; robust under the A_0-free convention; under the shifted convention A'_i=A_{i+1} this particular family does not give a counterexample, which is why the shift in the published disproof matters.
proposals.formal_interfaces: Trivial - quadratic discriminant in any proof assistant; Eulerian numbers A(3,k)=1,4,1.
proposals.duplicate_prior_status: sources/384757/aimpl-polypartition-p2.html, sources/384757/arxiv-2302.00754-abstract.html. The unshifted literal statement was not found explicitly resolved in sources inspected, but the adjacent shifted conjecture is publicly disproved; see objection.
proposals.strongest_routine_adaptation_objection: STRONG NOVELTY OBJECTION: the published literature already disproves Brenti's conjecture that the shifted Eulerian transformation A^o (x^n -> x A_n(x)) preserves real-rootedness on the same hypothesis class (Branden-Jochemko; see intro of arXiv:2302.00754, retained), and Athanasiadis (JLMS 2025) proved the positive family P_n[x] (nonnegative combinations of x^{n-k}(1+x)^k, containing all real-rooted polys with roots in [-1,0]). The unshifted counterexample above is a one-line variant of that public disproof phenomenon. RECOMMENDATION: do not allocate; park unless root judges the residual delta (explicit unshifted counterexample plus a classification of the maximal positive cone) non-derivative and worth a slot.
